skill.name: emailcampaignskill
skill.description: Plan, review, QA, and analyze email campaigns with clear audience checks, creative review, launch gates, and post-send retrospectives.
skill.summary: Guide email campaign planning, QA, launch readiness, and retrospective analysis.
skill.author: Sequenzy

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns in the three prompt-only files. Manual review found operational safety boundaries and no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, executable code, or requests to bypass review.

content.value_statement: Email campaigns can fail when briefs, audiences, creative, and launch checks are reviewed separately. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured workflow for campaign QA and analysis.
actual_capabilities: Builds campaign briefs with objective, audience, offer, send window, success metric, constraints, and approval owner.
Reviews audience logic for inclusions, exclusions, consent, suppression state, and expected recipient count.
Checks creative alignment across subject, preview, body, proof, CTA, landing page, and follow-up path.
Produces launch QA covering links, tracking, personalization, rendering, plain-text fallback, footer, and reply handling.
Analyzes post-send performance against baselines, segments, sources, and campaign hypotheses.
Separates recommendations from live execution and identifies approval gates for risky changes.
limitations: Does not send emails or change production systems on its own.
Does not replace legal, compliance, DNS, or sending authority review.
Requires accurate source material about audiences, consent, suppressions, and benchmarks.
Provider-specific guidance stays operational and may need current vendor documentation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Launch Brief
use_cases.description: Turn a campaign request into a clear brief with audience rules, success metrics, constraints, and approval ownership.

use_cases.title: Audit Audience and Creative
use_cases.description: Review segment logic, suppressions, consent, copy, links, tracking, and landing page alignment before launch.

use_cases.title: Run a Post-Send Retrospective
use_cases.description: Compare campaign results against baseline performance, segment behavior, deliverability context, and the original hypothesis.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Campaign Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an email campaign brief from this request. Include objective, audience, offer, send window, success metric, constraints, and approval owner.

prompt_templates.title: Review Audience Logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this audience plan for inclusions, exclusions, consent, suppressions, expected count, and risky assumptions. Return issues and approval questions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Creative and Launch Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this email campaign for promise match, CTA clarity, links, tracking, personalization, rendering, footer, reply handling, and launch blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Results and Recommend Next Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these campaign results against the baseline, segments, source, and hypothesis. Separate immediate fixes, future tests, and unresolved risks.

output_examples.input: Review a product announcement email before launch.
output: Launch decision: hold until audience suppression and landing page proof are confirmed.
Main risks: unclear offer ownership, missing unsubscribe footer check, and tracking gaps.
Next actions: confirm suppression count, test all links, and assign final approval owner.

output_examples.input: Analyze a campaign with low click rate and high unsubscribes.
output: Initial read: list quality and offer relevance need review before copy changes.
Compare performance by acquisition source, engagement age, and prior purchase status.
Next test: narrower audience, clearer promise, and a landing page aligned to one CTA.

best_practices: Provide the brief, audience rules, creative, links, tracking plan, and approval requirements together.
Validate consent, suppression logic, and expected recipient count before reviewing copy quality.
Separate recommendations from live-system actions and require approval for high-risk changes.
anti_patterns: Asking the skill to send email, import contacts, or edit suppressions without explicit approval.
Judging performance from one metric without baselines, segment context, or deliverability data.
Assuming missing consent, audience fields, legal approvals, or sending authority are acceptable.

faq.question: Can this skill send an email campaign?
faq.answer: No. It supports planning, review, QA, and analysis. Live sends require explicit human approval and platform access.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Provide the objective, offer, audience rules, creative, links, send timing, benchmarks, and approval requirements.

faq.question: Does it handle compliance review?
faq.answer: It can flag compliance questions, but it does not replace legal, privacy, or sending authority review.

faq.question: Can it review audience segments?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks inclusions, exclusions, consent, suppressions, expected count, and unclear assumptions.

faq.question: Can it help after a campaign sends?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports retrospectives that compare results against baselines, segments, sources, and hypotheses.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
